items.name: Extreme close-up
items.description: Frames a tiny part of the subject, such as the eyes, lips or a small object, filling the whole frame.
items.when_to_use: Moments of intense emotion, a crucial clue, or a detail the audience must not miss.
items.effect: Intimacy, tension and heightened intensity; can feel intrusive or abstract.

items.name: Close-up
items.description: Fills the frame with a face or a single object, cutting off everything below the chin or shoulders.
items.when_to_use: Reactions, emotional beats, key decisions and revealing what a character thinks or feels.
items.effect: Closeness and empathy; the viewer reads the character's inner state.

items.name: Medium close-up
items.description: Frames a person from roughly the chest or shoulders up, a step looser than a full close-up.
items.when_to_use: Conversations and interviews where you want intimacy without the intensity of a tight close-up.
items.effect: Comfortable closeness; keeps attention on expression while showing a little posture.

items.name: Medium shot
items.description: Shows a person from about the waist up, balancing face, gesture and a bit of surroundings.
items.when_to_use: General dialogue and action coverage; the everyday workhorse framing.
items.effect: Neutral, natural and conversational; feels like standing near someone.

items.name: Cowboy / American shot
items.description: Frames a person from about mid-thigh up, leaving room to see a holstered gun or hands at the hips.
items.when_to_use: Standoffs, confrontations and introductions of a confident or dangerous character.
items.effect: Posture and readiness to act; a sense of threat or swagger.

items.name: Medium long shot
items.description: Frames the subject from about the knees up, showing more body and some environment.
items.when_to_use: Walking-and-talking, moving action, and showing a character in their surroundings.
items.effect: Moderate distance with presence; body language begins to dominate over facial detail.

items.name: Full shot
items.description: Shows a person head to toe with little space above and below.
items.when_to_use: Introducing a character's costume and posture, dance, fights and physical action.
items.effect: Presence and physicality; the character is whole but still the focus.

items.name: Wide shot
items.description: Shows the subject small within a larger setting so location and relationships are clear.
items.when_to_use: Orienting the audience, group staging and showing how a character relates to a place.
items.effect: Context, scale and sometimes isolation or vulnerability.

items.name: Extreme wide shot
items.description: The subject is tiny or barely visible against a vast landscape or space.
items.when_to_use: Epic scenery, openings and endings, and emphasising how small a person is.
items.effect: Awe, loneliness or insignificance; strong sense of place.

items.name: Establishing shot
items.description: A wide framing, often at the start of a scene, that shows where and when the action takes place.
items.when_to_use: Opening a scene or sequence, and moving to a new location or time.
items.effect: Orients the viewer and sets mood before characters take over.

items.name: Two-shot
items.description: Frames two people together in one composition.
items.when_to_use: Showing a relationship, a shared reaction or a conversation without cutting.
items.effect: Connection or distance between characters, depending on how they are placed.

items.name: Group shot
items.description: Frames three or more people in one composition.
items.when_to_use: Ensemble scenes, meetings, family and team dynamics.
items.effect: Group dynamics, hierarchy and belonging or exclusion.

items.name: Over-the-shoulder
items.description: Camera sits behind one person, with their shoulder and head in the foreground, and frames the other person.
items.when_to_use: Dialogue, usually alternating between the two speakers.
items.effect: Connection and shared point of view; places the viewer in the conversation.

items.name: Insert shot
items.description: A close view of an object or detail that matters to the scene, such as a letter, phone or hand.
items.when_to_use: Showing information, props and actions the audience must read.
items.effect: Emphasis and clarity; directs attention and can build suspense.

items.name: Master shot
items.description: A single, usually wide take that covers the whole scene's action from start to end.
items.when_to_use: Coverage plan baseline; the shot the editor can fall back on for orientation.
items.effect: Clear geography and continuity of space and time.

items.name: Eye level
items.description: Camera is placed at the height of the subject's eyes, pointing straight ahead.
items.when_to_use: Default for natural dialogue and scenes that should feel neutral.
items.effect: Neutral, honest and relatable; the viewer sits on equal footing with the character.

items.name: High angle
items.description: Camera looks down on the subject from above eye level.
items.when_to_use: Making a character look small, weak or trapped, or showing the layout of a scene.
items.effect: Vulnerability, diminished status or being watched.

items.name: Low angle
items.description: Camera sits below the subject and looks up.
items.when_to_use: Heroes, villains, authority figures and anything that should feel imposing.
items.effect: Power, dominance, threat or heroism.

items.name: Bird's-eye view / overhead
items.description: Camera points straight down from directly above the scene.
items.when_to_use: Showing patterns and geography, choreography, or detaching from the action.
items.effect: Detachment, fate and a god-like or map-like view.

items.name: Worm's-eye view
items.description: Camera is at ground level or lower and points sharply up.
items.when_to_use: Making towering structures or people loom, or dramatic stylised moments.
items.effect: Extreme scale, awe or menace; disorienting.

items.name: Dutch angle / canted frame
items.description: Camera is tilted sideways so the horizon is not level.
items.when_to_use: Disorientation, madness, danger, or a world that has gone wrong.
items.effect: Unease, instability and psychological tension.

items.name: Shoulder level
items.description: Camera is at about shoulder height, a little lower than eye level.
items.when_to_use: Casual, observational coverage and walking scenes.
items.effect: Slightly informal and grounded; still reads as natural.

items.name: Hip level
items.description: Camera sits at about waist height, aimed forward or slightly up.
items.when_to_use: Showing hands, gestures or a holstered weapon, and giving a grounded look.
items.effect: Understated power and attention to physical action.

items.name: Knee level
items.description: Camera is placed near knee height, looking at the subject from low down.
items.when_to_use: Emphasising movement of legs and feet, or children's perspective.
items.effect: Tension from a slightly low viewpoint; adds a sense of motion.

items.name: Ground level
items.description: Camera rests on the ground, level with the floor.
items.when_to_use: Feet, vehicles and tracks passing, or a tiny creature's view.
items.effect: Immersion in the environment and low-down tension.

items.name: Point-of-view (POV) shot
items.description: The camera shows exactly what a character sees, as if through their eyes.
items.when_to_use: Discovery, fear, subjective experience and inviting the audience to identify.
items.effect: Identification and immersion; sharing the character's perception.

items.name: Aerial view
items.description: Camera is high above the ground, often from a drone, helicopter or plane.
items.when_to_use: Vast landscapes, chases and establishing location.
items.effect: Scale, freedom and an all-seeing perspective.

items.name: Profile angle
items.description: Camera sees the subject from the side, so the face is in profile.
items.when_to_use: Showing contemplation, interaction between two facing characters, or silhouette-like drama.
items.effect: Detachment, reflection or an observational feel.

items.name: Static shot
items.description: The camera is locked off and does not move; action moves within the frame.
items.when_to_use: Calm scenes, precise compositions and letting performance play out.
items.effect: Stability, observation and tension through stillness.

items.name: Pan
items.description: Camera rotates horizontally left or right from a fixed position.
items.when_to_use: Following a subject, surveying a space or linking two things in the scene.
items.effect: Reveals space gradually; connects subjects and guides attention.

items.name: Tilt
items.description: Camera rotates vertically up or down from a fixed position.
items.when_to_use: Revealing the height of a person or building, or following vertical movement.
items.effect: Reveals scale and creates a sense of awe or discovery.

items.name: Whip pan
items.description: A very fast pan that blurs the image between two points.
items.when_to_use: Sudden attention shifts, transitions and comic or frantic energy.
items.effect: Urgency, surprise and kinetic energy.

items.name: Dolly in / push in
items.description: Camera physically moves forward toward the subject on a dolly or similar support.
items.when_to_use: Building tension, emphasising a realisation or drawing the audience into a character.
items.effect: Growing intimacy, focus and rising emotion.

items.name: Dolly out / pull out
items.description: Camera moves backward away from the subject.
items.when_to_use: Revealing context, ending a scene, or showing isolation.
items.effect: Distance, release, revelation or loneliness.

items.name: Truck
items.description: Camera moves sideways, left or right, parallel to the subject.
items.when_to_use: Following walking characters or moving along a row of objects or people.
items.effect: Smooth lateral flow and a sense of accompanying the character.

items.name: Pedestal
items.description: Camera moves straight up or down while staying level and pointed the same way.
items.when_to_use: Revealing something above or below, or shifting height without tilting.
items.effect: Subtle reveal and change of perspective without changing the view direction.

items.name: Crane / jib shot
items.description: Camera is mounted on an arm that swings and raises or lowers it through space.
items.when_to_use: Grand openings and closings, rising away from a scene, or sweeping reveals.
items.effect: Scale, grandeur and a sense of looking over the world.

items.name: Handheld
items.description: Camera is held by the operator without a stabiliser, producing natural shake.
items.when_to_use: Documentary realism, chaotic action and raw, immediate scenes.
items.effect: Urgency, realism and anxiety; viewer feels present in the scene.

items.name: Steadicam / gimbal
items.description: A stabilised rig lets the operator move smoothly through a space with a floating look.
items.when_to_use: Long walking takes, following characters through corridors and complex spaces.
items.effect: Fluid, immersive and dreamlike motion that lets viewers glide with the action.

items.name: Zoom
items.description: Lens focal length changes to make the subject appear closer or farther without moving the camera.
items.when_to_use: Quick emphasis, surveillance looks, retro styles and documentary feel.
items.effect: Sudden attention or voyeurism; flatter than a dolly move.

items.name: Dolly zoom / vertigo effect
items.description: Camera dollies one way while the lens zooms the opposite way, so the subject stays the same size but the background stretches or compresses.
items.when_to_use: Moments of shock, realisation, dread or a world warping around a character.
items.effect: Disorientation and psychological vertigo.

items.name: Arc shot
items.description: Camera circles around the subject along a curved path.
items.when_to_use: Dramatic reveals, romantic moments and showing a character from many sides.
items.effect: Energy, intensity and importance; the subject feels the centre of the world.

items.name: Tracking shot
items.description: Camera travels alongside, ahead of or behind a moving subject on tracks, dolly or rig.
items.when_to_use: Following a character through a space, chases and long takes.
items.effect: Momentum and immersion; keeps the viewer with the subject.

items.name: Aerial / drone move
items.description: Camera flies through the air on a drone, helicopter or similar platform.
items.when_to_use: Sweeping landscapes, high-speed chases and large-scale reveals.
items.effect: Freedom, scale and spectacle.

items.name: Reveal move (push-through)
items.description: A camera move that passes an obstacle or turns a corner to uncover a new subject.
items.when_to_use: Surprise reveals and spatial transitions within one take.
items.effect: Surprise and a sense of discovery.

items.name: Snorricam
items.description: Camera is strapped to the actor's body, so the face stays fixed while the world moves.
items.when_to_use: Intoxication, panic or psychological breakdown.
items.effect: Disorientation seen from inside the character's body.
